Steady states by pseudo-transient continuation

Source: vignettes/articles/methods-ptc.Rmd
methods-ptc.Rmd

ptc() solves for a steady state by pseudo-transient continuation. dMod2 calls the same solver from C++ for Pimpl() through cppde_ptc_v1. Notation; \(x\) are the solved variables of a cppFUN() object, \(f(x, p)\) the paired outputs.

Steady-state problem

ptc() solves

\[G(x) = \begin{pmatrix} f(x, p) \\ C x - b \end{pmatrix} = 0 , \tag{1}\]

with \(C\) the constraint matrix and \(b\) the argument total. For a reaction network the rows of \(C\) are conserved quantities, and (1) selects one root per value of \(b\). With flow = TRUE (default), \(f\) is the right-hand side of \(\dot x = f(x, p)\) and the solver seeks a stable steady state, not any root.

Continuation step

With \(I_f\) the identity on the rows of \(f\) and zero on the rows of \(C\), every step solves

\[\left(\frac{I_f}{\Delta t} - \frac{\partial G}{\partial x}\right) d = G(x) \tag{2}\]

for the step \(d\) [1], [2]. For small \(\Delta t\), (2) is an implicit Euler step of \(\dot x = f\) on \(C x = b\); for \(\Delta t \to \infty\) it is Newton’s method on (1). Far from the root, where Newton’s method could jump to an unstable root or leave the positive orthant, the iteration follows the flow; near it, convergence is quadratic. QR solves (2) in the least-squares sense, rows scaled by the residual scale of (4), columns by \(|x_i| + \mathrm{abstol}\).

  • positive = TRUE (default): the update \(x_i \exp(d_i / x_i)\), \(x + d\) to first order, exponent capped at \(\pm\)zmax, projected back onto \(C x = b\) by \(x \exp(C^\mathsf{T} \mu)\), \(\mu\) from a damped Newton iteration.
  • flow = FALSE: the step follows the Newton flow, \(d = -(\partial G/\partial x)^{+} G \, \Delta t / (1 + \Delta t)\), to any regular root.

Pseudo-time step control

The first step is \(\Delta t_0 = \mathrm{dtInit} / \max_i |J_{ii}|\) with flow = TRUE, \(\mathrm{dtInit}\) otherwise. The local error of an implicit Euler step is estimated as

\[e = \left(\frac{I_f}{\Delta t} - \frac{\partial G}{\partial x}\right)^{-1} \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac12 \bigl(f(x + d, p) - f(x, p)\bigr) \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} , \tag{3}\]

in the root mean square of \(e_i / (\mathrm{flowTol}\,|x_i| + \mathrm{abstol})\). A step with error above 1 is repeated at smaller \(\Delta t\). After an accepted step, \(\Delta t\) changes by the residual ratio (2 to 1000) if the residual has halved, otherwise by the error-estimate factor (0.2 to 10). In the Newton range, \(\Delta t \ge 10^8 / \max_i |J_{ii}|\), a step halving the residual is accepted regardless of the error. In the flow range the error decides alone, since such a step can still leave the basin of the stable root.

Convergence test

Row \(i\) of (1) has converged when

\[|G_i| \le \mathrm{reltol} \sum_k \left|\frac{\partial G_i}{\partial x_k}\right| |x_k| + \mathrm{abstol} \max_k \left|\frac{\partial G_i}{\partial x_k}\right| , \tag{4}\]

the residual against the turnover of the row, the sum of the rates that cancel in it, so the test scales with the rates of the row. In the Newton range, a step below \(\mathrm{reltol}\,|x_i| + \mathrm{abstol}\) in every variable also ends the iteration. Contracting Newton steps then bring every variable to within \(\mathrm{reltol}\,(|x_i| + \mathrm{abstol})\) of the root. Equal start, parameters and controls return the same root to the last digit.

Stability test

With \(N\) an orthonormal kernel basis of \(C\) from the singular value decomposition, the flow on \(C x = b\) near the root has the Jacobian

\[B = N^\mathsf{T} J N , \tag{5}\]

and the root is stable if every eigenvalue of \(B\) has negative real part. With stability = TRUE (default, flow = TRUE only), ptc() accepts the root while the leading eigenvalue satisfies \(\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda \le \max(10^{-8} \max_k |\lambda_k|, \mathrm{stabilityTol})\). A small positive stabilityTol accepts a root that perturbations leave slower than a time scale of interest, as near a Hopf bifurcation.

From an unstable root \(x^*\) the search restarts at \(x^* \pm \eta v\), \(v\) the real part of the leading eigenvector mapped back by \(N\), first on the side the iterates came from while they followed the flow (\(\Delta t\, \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda < 1\)). \(\eta\) moves every variable by at most a tenth of the variable value. Near \(x^*\), \(\Delta t \le 1 / (2\,\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda)\), so the implicit Euler step leaves along the unstable direction, where Newton’s method would return. The new root is tested again; if neither side leads to a stable root, ptc() reports the unstable one, leading eigenvalue in message.

References

[1]
C. T. Kelley and D. E. Keyes, “Convergence analysis of pseudo-transient continuation,” SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis, vol. 35, no. 2, pp. 508–523, 1998.
[2]
T. S. Coffey, C. T. Kelley, and D. E. Keyes, “Pseudotransient continuation and differential-algebraic equations,” SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing, vol. 25, no. 2, pp. 553–569, 2003.
